key_insight: An invariant neural-network closure recovers two-equation RANS turbulence behavior in coarse-mesh reactor simulations without solving turbulence transport equations.
engineering_relevance: The closure improves molten-salt reactor flow predictions at system-code cost, taking about 0.2 core-hours versus 330 core-hours for Nek5000 in the reported transient.
method: Predict turbulent kinetic energy and timescale from neighboring flow and geometry, with exact invariance to translation, Galilean boosts, rotation, reflection, and neighbor ordering.
Insert non-negative eddy viscosity into SAM’s implicit diffusion operator to maintain well-conditioned momentum equations.
Iteratively retrain on SAM flow states against fixed Nek5000 targets to reduce coarse-mesh covariate shift.
evidence_signal: On a held-out steady state, the closure reproduces the reference recirculation cell and eddy-viscosity plume; during a 120 s pump coastdown, velocity error falls from 37.6% to 17.7%, with 12% time-averaged relative eddy-viscosity error.
watch_item: Coarse-mesh resolution remains a source of velocity error, and accuracy beyond the reported MSFR cases is not established.
paper_title: An Invariant Neural-Network Eddy-Viscosity Closure with Iterative Solver Coupling for Molten Salt Fast Reactor Thermal-Hydraulics
